evals.prompt: The episode master is ep03_master_v02.mp4 and the takes passed dialogue QA. Build English and Spanish subtitle sidecars from the locked lines. The second clip starts at 17.4 s on the Studio timeline.
evals.expected_output: Names the sidecars correctly, applies the clip offset and keeps subtitles out of the video.
expectations: Names the files ep03_master_v02.en.srt and ep03_master_v02.es.srt.
Uses the locked dialogue text, with transcript output used only for timing.
Sets the second clip's offset to 17.4 s from the Studio start, not from planned durations.
Delivers a sidecar and does not burn subtitles into generated video.

evals.prompt: Make Mandarin subtitles for a 9:16 episode. One line is long and has commas and a full stop.
evals.expected_output: Wraps by character with narrow lines and keeps punctuation off line starts.
expectations: Uses a narrow line width for Chinese, around 16 characters, and at most two lines.
Breaks between characters without a line starting on closing punctuation.
Splits an overlong line into several cues with time shared by text length.
Uses the zh code in the filename.

evals.prompt: Add Arabic subtitles. One speaker line also contains a short Latin-script phrase. How do you make sure the lines display correctly?
evals.expected_output: Handles right-to-left wrapping and flags the mixed-direction check as unverified until seen in a player.
expectations: Wraps at spaces only and never inside a word or combining-mark cluster.
Adds a leading right-to-left mark to each line.
Treats mixed-direction display as unverified until viewed in a real player.
Names the sidecar with the ar language code.

evals.prompt: The French line is missing from the dialogue file but I need the fr sidecar today, and the actor said a different word in take 2 so match the subtitle to what was said.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to invent text and refuses to follow the heard word.
expectations: Reports the missing fr text for the named line instead of generating a partial file.
Asks for locked or approved French text rather than machine-guessing it silently.
Keeps the locked word in the subtitle and records the spoken difference as a take defect.
Does not edit the sidecar to match the heard word.
